target_moa.text: Lusutrombopag is a small-molecule thrombopoietin (TPO) receptor agonist that acts on the transmembrane domain of human TPO receptors expressed on megakaryocytes, inducing proliferation and differentiation of megakaryocytic progenitor cells and megakaryocyte maturation, resulting in increased platelet production

citations.quote: Mechanism of Action	Lusutrombopag is a small molecule TPO receptor agonist that acts on the transmembrane domain of human TPO receptors expressed on megakaryocytes to induce the proliferation and differentiation of megakaryocytic progenitor cells from hematopoietic stem cells and megakaryocyte maturation.

Lusutrombopag is a small molecule thrombopoietin (TPO) receptor agonist that binds to the transmembrane domain of the human TPO receptors to stimulate megakaryocyte proliferation and differentiation, which results in increased platelet production.

key_safety.text: Generally well tolerated; the most common adverse reaction (≥3%) was headache (5% MULPLETA vs 4% placebo). Serious adverse events occurred in 5% (9/171) of MULPLETA vs 7% (12/170) placebo; the most common serious adverse reaction was portal vein thrombosis. Thromboembolic AESIs were reported in 6 patients (1.8%) on lusutrombopag and 4 (1.2%) on placebo.

The incidence of serious adverse events was 5% (9 of 171 patients) in the MULPLETA group and 7% (12 of 170 patients) in the placebo group. The most common serious adverse reaction reported with MULPLETA was portal vein thrombosis [see *Warnings and Precautions* (5.1)]. No adverse reactions resulted in discontinuation of MULPLETA.
In the thromboembolic category, treatment emergent AESIs were reported in 6 patients (1.8%) in the lusutrombopag arm and 4 patients (1.2%) in the placebo group.
